purpose: Paired authoring examples with grounded reviewer dispositions. Application paths/commands are illustrative; structural tests are not semantic judgment or application execution.

task.description: Improve the marker interaction. Choose what looks best.

reasons: Neither target replacement nor interruption behavior is selected. Two incompatible implementations could satisfy this wording.
Whitespace checks provide no observable motion evidence.
review.next: Specify behavior for retargeting, cancellation and reduced motion, then choose matching runtime proof.

task.summary: Retarget from the current displayed position
task.description: Accepted: a new target replaces the old target immediately and starts at the currently displayed position. Idle/travelling/cancelled states: cancellation freezes the current position; the next target resumes from there. Reduced motion jumps directly to the latest target. Delegated: choose 120–180 ms duration and record it. No changes to input bindings or persistence.
acceptance: Retargeting halfway through travel neither returns to the start nor visits the old target.
Cancellation freezes position; repeated identical targets do not restart travel.
Reduced motion reaches the latest target without animation.
verification: Run the demo at normal and reduced-motion settings; retain before/after capture and inspected frame timestamps.

reasons: Target replacement, cancellation and reduced motion have observable outcomes; tuning has a bounded delegated range.
Unit checks and relevant runtime/frame evidence match the state behavior. Readiness is an authoring assessment, not proof that the application works.
review.next: Execute within scope; implementation outcomes remain pending until actual runtime checks and critic evidence exist.

task.description: Unresolved: replace the old target immediately or queue the new target. Owner: product owner. Gate: accept retarget-rule before dependent implementation. No actor has accepted this rule yet.
acceptance: Movement follows the selected retarget rule.

reasons: The unresolved choice changes user-visible behavior; it is not a numeric tuning parameter.
The explicit retarget-rule reference connects the dependency to the existing claim/finish gate even for local impact.
review.next: Research alternatives if necessary and obtain the authorized decision; dependent implementation remains open.

task.summary: Tune travel duration within the accepted behavior
task.description: Accepted behavior: latest target replaces the previous target from the current position. Delegated to implementer: choose one duration in 120–180 ms and record the measured result; do not change retargeting behavior.
acceptance: The chosen duration lies in 120–180 ms and retargeting behavior remains unchanged.
verification: Inspect a runtime capture with frame timestamps.

reasons: The semantic rule is fixed; the remaining choice is bounded, reversible timing delegated to the implementer.
Runtime evidence measures the timing and tests preserve the behavior. No separate user approval or new decision record is required.
review.next: Choose, measure and record the duration during execution.

task.description: Reported: marker sometimes snaps during rapid clicking. No reproduction has been obtained; root cause is unknown. A timing hypothesis is recorded but unverified.
acceptance: The reported jump is reproduced and a regression demonstrates that the cause is corrected.
verification: Replay the captured failing input sequence before and after the correction.

reasons: The requested outcome is a verified correction; no failing sequence or causal evidence exists yet.
A hypothesis document, successful process or unrelated passing test cannot prove this fix.
review.next: Reproduce and investigate in a bounded research scope. Keep the original fix outcome pending/blocked until correction evidence exists.

task.description: Research-only scope. Compare immediate replacement and queued movement using disposable observations. Produce a recommendation with trade-offs and unresolved choices for the product owner; do not select a production rule or edit app code.
acceptance: A comparison states observed trade-offs, source references, unresolved choices and the next decision owner.
verification: Review docs/retarget-research.md against the experiment notes and both alternatives.

reasons: Open choices are the subject of the research deliverable, not implementation authority.
The modify scope contains only the research report. Readiness applies only to the research task; it does not unblock a dependent implementation task.
review.next: Complete research evidence; dependent implementation must use a real execution dependency and/or the explicit governing decision.

task.description: Change “teh marker” to “the marker” in the README; preserve meaning and all other content.
acceptance: README contains “the marker” where “teh marker” appeared.
verification: Inspect the one-line diff and run git diff --check.

reasons: One concrete before/after change and a proportionate diff check are sufficient.
No runtime, video, audio, architecture brief or new approval is relevant.
review.next: Make the one-line fix and inspect it.

task.description: Existing task without execution_contract or architecture metadata. Its historical dependency note is not an enforced lifecycle edge.
acceptance: The task retains its existing workflow semantics.

reasons: Compatibility concerns structural loading and unchanged legacy claim behavior. It is not a blanket semantic readiness certificate for every old task.
A new consequential use needs content review and explicit lifecycle adoption before relying on executable dependency fields.
review.next: Preserve history. Review and explicitly adopt policy when new consequential execution requires it.
